title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Garden Auditorium on 1966-07-29

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard recording of a scorching July 29 1966 Vancouver set – hot Cardboard Cowboy, Baby Blue, Viola Lee Blues and early‑Dead energy.
ai_review.review: The show is hailed as a landmark early‑Dead performance with smoking renditions of Cardcardboard Cowboy (The Monster), Baby Blue, Viola Lee Blues, Standing on the Corner and Cream Puff War.  The soundboard source delivers surprisingly clear audio for 1966 – a little hiss but overall excellent clarity that lets Jerry’s guitar tone and Pigpen’s organ roar through.  Energy is consistently high, making this a must‑listen snapshot of the band’s formative psychedelic era.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews (majority 5‑star) praise both the performance and audio fidelity; many specific song highlights and technical compliments support a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp sound for a mid‑60s tape with only mild hiss and occasional fuzziness; audience is barely audible but the mix is well balanced and showcases guitars and organ.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑Dead set flows through classic folk‑rock numbers into psychedelic jams, with tight transitions and a high‑energy second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's tone is described as perfect on Baby Blue and Next Time You See Me; his playing is highlighted throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s high vocal harmonies on Viola Lee Blues are praised; a few reviewers note his bass work but no specific solo comments.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob is noted as being low in the mix but otherwise present.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen's organ is repeatedly called out as ripping, cranked and a key driver of the early psychedelic sound.
